video_title: We get HEATED if this is LeBron's best roster and if he can ACTUALLY catch up to Michael Jordan 👀

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson and Raymond Felton discuss LeBron James joining the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: LeBron James will be headed to the Philadelphia 76ers

text_blocks.speaker: Theo Pinson
text_blocks.text: What were your thoughts when you saw it?

text_blocks.speaker: Raymond Felton
text_blocks.text: Ill. First thing came to mind. It looks nasty.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton evaluates the talent level of the 76ers roster
quotes.excerpt: This might be the best team ever he's been on, constructed one.
quotes.quote: This might be the best team ever he's been on, constructed one. Rather than the Miami Heat team. It has the most talent, I think. It is the most talented team he's ever been on. It's not even close.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson questions the impact of LeBron's decision on his legacy
quotes.excerpt: What does this mean for LeBron's legacy?

text_blocks.speaker: Theo Pinson
text_blocks.text: What does this mean for LeBron's legacy in your eyes?

text_blocks.speaker: Raymond Felton
text_blocks.text: His legacy's been written, fam. Nothing he does will change his legacy. He wins another chip, great. He's still not better than Mike. And if he doesn't win one, great. He's still a Hall of Famer, arguably the second or third best player ever.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton argues LeBron should have returned to Cleveland
quotes.excerpt: He should have went to Cleveland because it's just better for the story.
quotes.quote: He should have went to Cleveland because it's just better for the story. The narrative is better of him going to Cleveland. And if he wins one in Cleveland, that's a perfect way to just end it, fam, right there.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson challenges the pressure of LeBron's championship expectations
quotes.excerpt: You put the pressure back on yourself.

text_blocks.speaker: Theo Pinson
text_blocks.text: Now he's went to Philly, now what? Because you have put it out there that you are going to win. You put the pressure back on yourself. This shit matters.

text_blocks.speaker: Raymond Felton
text_blocks.text: Wherever LeBron was going, there's a good chance for them to win.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton ranks LeBron among the greatest players of all time
quotes.excerpt: He's still a top three player in the world.
quotes.quote: He's still a Hall of Famer, arguably the second, third best player ever. Top three players in the world.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson recalls Rich Paul's comments on LeBron's potential move to New York
quotes.excerpt: If the Knicks did not win this year, he was going to New York.

text_blocks.speaker: Theo Pinson
text_blocks.text: When Rich Paul went on that motherfucker, it said, look, if the Knicks did not win this year, he was going to New York. Why? Because he knew he was, if he joined that team, they would have had a chance to win.

text_blocks.speaker: Raymond Felton
text_blocks.text: Now he's like, what's the best Knicks scenario? The Philadelphia 76ers. They haven't won since 1983.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton lists Michael Jordan's statistical advantages over LeBron
quotes.excerpt: Let me tell you what Jordan is number one in still to this day: points per game.
quotes.quote: Let me tell you what Jordan is number one in still to this day: points per game, playoffs points per game, scoring titles, Finals MVP, all defensive first teams, player efficiency rating, playoffs per win shares. He's in first in a lot of categories still.

quotes.speaker: Charlie Villanueva
quotes.summary_phrase: Charlie Villanueva evaluates Michael Jordan and LeBron James's playing styles
quotes.excerpt: Jordan is probably the most dominant player we've seen. LeBron is the most all-around player.
quotes.quote: Jordan is probably the most dominant player we've seen. LeBron is the most all-around player we've seen, and the healthiest that we've been able to see. That's why he's been able to play longer. He's been able to dominate the game longer because of his ability, his all-around ability.
